fatal_errors: The starting material is incorrectly described as an existing W–Cu composite. The target starts from a directionally segregated WTaVTi alloy, whose Ti/V-rich interdendritic channels are replaced by Cu.
The hypothesis treats Ti as a phase added to a W–Cu composite rather than an intrinsic sacrificial constituent of the WTaVTi precursor.
It omits the essential 1200 °C, 96 h molten-Cu treatment and therefore does not reconstruct the demonstrated processing window.
The mechanism incorrectly invokes reorganization of W into ligaments; the RHEA dendritic network is retained while Cu selectively replaces Ti-rich interdendritic material.
The W-rich approximately 300 nm passivating interlayer, central to stable RHEA–Cu bonding and arrest of further exchange, is omitted.

Irradiation performance is asserted for the treated composite even though the target evidence comes from 25 keV He+ tests on precursor dendrites as a proxy, not direct irradiation of the finished composite.
explanation: The response identifies the broad intervention—liquid-metal dealloying in molten Cu using Ti-rich sacrificial regions—and predicts improved conductivity through an aligned conductive architecture. However, it reconstructs the wrong initial material and oversimplifies selective replacement as Ti removal and W reorganization. It misses Ta/V-containing RHEA ligaments, Cu exchange, the W-rich interfacial layer, quantitative phase fractions, and all decisive processing and service conditions. The outcome is only qualitative and conflates thermal and irradiation evidence; it omits the measured temperature dependence, crossover above roughly 650 °C, and the limited proxy nature of the He+ results. The proposed control experiment is somewhat discriminating but changes both precursor composition and processing, lacks a dealloyed control architecture, and gives no specified thermal or irradiation conditions. No supporting evidence is supplied.
